---
title: "Predict GEBV for New Individuals Using a Fitted masreml Model"
---

## Predict GEBV for New Individuals Using a Fitted masreml Model {.unnumbered}


### Description

Computes genomic estimated breeding values (GEBV) for test individuals
using the relationship between test and training sets. Two modes are
supported: pre-built G matrix (full or cross-block) and raw marker data.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>## S3 method for class 'masreml'
predict(
  object,
  G_full = NULL,
  markers_new = NULL,
  markers_train = NULL,
  train_ids = NULL,
  test_ids = NULL,
  y_new = NULL,
  X_new = NULL,
  link = NULL,
  jitter = 1e-06,
  ...
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="object">object</code></td>
<td>
fitted <code>masreml</code> object from <code>masreml()</code>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="G_full">G_full</code></td>
<td>
numeric matrix (n_total x n_total), pre-built genomic
relationship matrix including both training and test individuals.
Row/column names must include all training IDs and test IDs.
Either <code>G_full</code> or <code>markers_new</code> must be provided.
For multi-component models, provide a named list of G matrices,
one per component (names must match <code>names(object\$gebv)</code>).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="markers_new">markers_new</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker data for test individuals only.
Used to compute cross-G matrix <code>G[test, train]</code> directly
from marker data. Supported elements:


<ul>
<li> <code>snp_add</code>: integer matrix (n_test x m), raw genotype 0/1/2

</li>
<li> <code>mh_add</code>: list of data.frames in same format as
<code>build_G_mh()</code> input (one per chromosome, first col = ID)

</li></ul>

Allele frequencies and scaling factors are computed from training
markers stored via <code>markers_train</code> argument.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="markers_train">markers_train</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker data for training individuals,
required when <code>markers_new</code> is provided. Same format as
<code>markers_new</code>. Used to compute consistent allele frequencies
and scaling (k) for cross-G computation.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="train_ids">train_ids</code></td>
<td>
character vector of training individual IDs, in the
same order as used when fitting <code>object</code>. Required when using
<code>G_full</code> mode to subset the training block.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="test_ids">test_ids</code></td>
<td>
character vector of test individual IDs. Required for
<code>G_full</code> mode. Inferred from <code>markers_new</code> row names if
not provided.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y_new">y_new</code></td>
<td>
optional numeric vector of observed phenotypes for test
individuals. When supplied, prediction metrics (R2, RMSE, accuracy
or AUC, bias) are computed automatically and stored in
<code>\$metrics</code>. For binary, metrics are on the observed
(probability) scale so <code>bias</code> is the calibration slope.
Length must match the number of test individuals.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X_new">X_new</code></td>
<td>
optional numeric matrix of fixed-effects design for test
individuals (n_test x c). Required only if the original fit used
non-intercept fixed effects. Defaults to an intercept column of 1s.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="link">link</code></td>
<td>
character, link function for binary trait prediction:
<code>"logit"</code> (default) or <code>"probit"</code>. Inherited from
<code>object\$binary\$link</code> if available.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="jitter">jitter</code></td>
<td>
numeric, small value added to diagonal of
<code>G[train,train]</code> for numerical stability (default 1e-6).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
ignored
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

The prediction formula per component k is:

<p style="text-align: center;">$\hat{u}_{test,k} = G_{te,tr,k} \cdot (G_{tr,tr,k} + \lambda_k I)^{-1} \cdot \hat{u}_{train,k}$


where $\lambda_k = \sigma^2_e / \sigma^2_{g,k}$.

For <code>markers_new</code> mode (SNP), the cross-G is:

<p style="text-align: center;">$G_{te,tr} = \frac{W_{te} W_{tr}'}{k}$


where $W$ matrices are centered using training allele frequencies
and $k = \sum 2p_j(1-p_j)$ computed from training data.

For binary trait, prediction is on the liability scale. Fitted
probabilities are obtained by applying the inverse link function
to $\eta_{test} = \mu_{fixed} + \hat{u}_{test}$.



### Value

list of class <code>"masreml_pred"</code>. Field names are aligned
with <code>masbayes::predict.masbayes_*()</code> for cross-package
workflows. Backward-compatibility aliases (<code>total_gebv</code>,
<code>fitted</code>) are retained.


<ul>
<li> <code>GEBV</code>: named numeric vector of total GEBV for test
individuals (sum across components). Liability scale for binary.

</li>
<li> <code>total_gebv</code>: alias for <code>GEBV</code> (back-compat).

</li>
<li> <code>gebv</code>: named list of per-component GEBV vectors.

</li>
<li> <code>prob</code>: fitted probabilities <code>P(y=1)</code> for binary
trait via inverse-link, <code>NULL</code> for continuous.

</li>
<li> <code>fitted</code>: alias for <code>prob</code> (back-compat).

</li>
<li> <code>metrics</code>: list of test-set metrics if <code>y_new</code>
supplied (R2, RMSE, accuracy/AUC, bias), else <code>NULL</code>.

</li>
<li> <code>h2, sigma2</code>: heritability and variance components
carried over from the fit.

</li>
<li> <code>response_type</code>: <code>"continuous"</code> or <code>"binary"</code>.

</li>
<li> <code>algorithm</code>: REML algorithm from the fit.

</li>
<li> <code>eval_scope</code>: <code>"in-sample (training)"</code>,
<code>"test set (G_full)"</code>, or <code>"test set (markers_new)"</code>.

</li>
<li> <code>has_truth</code>: <code>TRUE</code> if metrics were computed.

</li>
<li> <code>train_ids, test_ids</code>: ID vectors.

</li>
<li> <code>n_train, n_test</code>: sample sizes.

</li></ul>



### See Also

<code>masreml</code>, <code>build_G_snp</code>,
<code>build_G_mh</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masreml")

d       <- load_data("small")
W       <- d$snp
y       <- d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_snp; names(y) <- d$pheno$id
W_train <- W[d$train_idx, ]
W_test  <- W[d$test_idx, ]
y_train <- y[d$train_idx]
y_test  <- y[d$test_idx]

# ── In-sample mode: shortcut to training metrics ──────────
fit  <- masreml(y_train, markers = list(snp_add = W_train))
pred <- predict(fit)               # no test data → returns training info
pred$metrics                       # = fit$training_metrics

# ── G_full pre-built, with auto-metrics ───────────────────
G_full <- build_G_snp(W, ref_W = W_train)
G_tr   <- G_full[rownames(W_train), rownames(W_train)]
fit_g  <- masreml(y_train, G = list(snp_add = G_tr))
pred_g <- predict(fit_g,
  G_full    = list(snp_add = G_full),
  train_ids = rownames(W_train),
  test_ids  = rownames(W_test),
  y_new     = y_test)
pred_g$metrics$accuracy

# ── markers_new + auto-metrics ────────────────────────────
pred_m <- predict(fit,
  markers_new   = list(snp_add = W_test),
  markers_train = list(snp_add = W_train),
  y_new         = y_test)
pred_m$metrics$bias

# ── Forecast only (no y_new) ──────────────────────────────
fc <- predict(fit, markers_new = list(snp_add = W_test),
                   markers_train = list(snp_add = W_train))
head(fc$GEBV)                      # metrics is NULL




```
